title: Multi-second main-thread stalls (100% CPU in Windows message pump) while mouse cursor is visible — regression from 4.7.1 to 4.7.2
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: **4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]**
- Not reproducible in: **4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]** (same project, same machine, same session pattern — reverting only the engine binary removes the problem completely)

### System information

Windows 11 Pro (build 10.0.26200) - Godot 4.7.2.stable - Forward+ - **D3D12** - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (581.80 / 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D (16 threads) - 144 Hz display, vsync enabled

### Issue description

After upgrading a mid-size 3D game from 4.7.1 to 4.7.2, the game's main thread periodically stalls for **0.3–4 seconds per frame**, in episodes lasting 20–90 seconds that recover on their own. The trigger correlates 100 % with **`Input.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE` + the mouse being moved** (i.e., fullscreen UI menus; during gameplay the cursor is captured and the problem never occurs). The first menu open after launch is typically clean; later opens (after 1–2 minutes of active play) freeze within a fraction of a second of the cursor becoming visible. Reproduces identically in editor-run games and exported builds.

I instrumented this fairly heavily before realizing it was a regression, so here is what is known:

**Where the time goes.** Per-frame engine-stage timing (via `physics_frame` / `process_frame` / `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` / `frame_post_draw` signals plus a max-`process_priority` node) shows ~99 % of each multi-second frame elapses **between `frame_post_draw` and the first stage of the next iteration** — i.e., inside `DisplayServerWindows::process_events()`. Everything else stays tiny during the stall:

```
frame 2107 ms = between-frames 2096.5   (1 InputEventMouseMotion delivered, arrived 2096 ms after post_draw)
              + physics 8 steps (scripts 4.2 / engine 1.0)
              + process (scripts 0.9 / deferred 3.4)
              + render 1.0
```

`Performance.TIME_PROCESS` ≈ 1–7 ms, viewport render times ≈ 0.1–0.5 ms CPU/GPU, pipeline-compilation counters flat, physics step ~1 ms (the 8 steps/frame are a consequence of the long frame, not the cause).

**The main thread is busy, not blocked.** A watchdog thread inside the process keeps ticking at its normal 2–3 ms during the stalls (only the main thread is affected). Wait Chain Traversal on the main thread shows no wait chain at all — thread state `Running`, burning **100 % of one core continuously** (+156–172 ms CPU per 150 ms wall-clock, for the whole episode).

**Where it spins.** External stack sampling (SuspendThread + GetThreadContext every 200 ms, offsets resolved against export tables) during the stalls:

- ~35 % of samples: RIP in `win32u!NtUserPeekMessage`, stack through `user32!PeekMessageW` / `TranslateMessage` / `DispatchMessageW` / `CallWindowProcW` into low `Godot.exe` offsets (the `process_events` pump loop / WndProc);
- the rest: `win32u!NtUserGetProp2` (via `GetPropW`), `NtUserIsTopLevelWindow`, `NtUserIsNonClientDpiScalingEnabled`, `GetSystemMetrics`, `EnumDisplayMonitors`, and `uxtheme.dll` internals near `GetImmersiveUserColorSetPreference` (per-message themed-window processing).

So the pump loop appears to be dispatching an enormous number of messages (or re-processing the same ones) at full speed for seconds at a time, while only ~1 coalesced mouse-motion `InputEvent` per frame actually reaches the scene.

**Ruled out by measurement** (each with a dedicated probe):

- foreign code in-process: module list contains only Windows + NVIDIA UMD (no overlays/hooks); Wacom `wintab32.dll` stub present but reproduced with `pen_tablet/driver = winink` as well, where `Wacom_Tablet.dll` is not loaded;
- system-wide broadcast storms: a separate witness top-level window received **zero** `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` / `WM_THEMECHANGED` / `WM_DEVICECHANGE` during the freezes;
- raw-input device flood: the witness window registered for the same raw input (mouse + pen usages, `RIDEV_INPUTSINK`) saw a normal 15–120 `WM_INPUT`/s during the freezes;
- `WM_PAINT` invalidation loop: `GetUpdateRect` on the game window was dirty in only 3 of 381 samples;
- cross-process `SendMessage`/ALPC waits: wait chain empty (see above);
- GPU/driver, shader/pipeline compilation, physics, GDScript: all measured flat (see above).

**Suspect area (speculation):** 4.7.2 reworked Windows mouse input handling (high-polling-rate improvements). Given the exact trigger (visible cursor + mouse movement) and the pump-bound profile, that change is where I would look first. Mouse is a regular ~1000 Hz gaming mouse; a Wacom tablet driver is installed (but see above — reproduced with `winink` and normal WinTab alike).

### Steps to reproduce

No minimal project yet, and the failure needs a few minutes of preceding gameplay, which suggests some accumulating state:

1. 3D game (Forward+, D3D12, vsync on), mouse captured during gameplay (`MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED`).
2. Play actively for ~1–2 minutes (spawning/freeing nodes, audio, UI updates).
3. Open a fullscreen `Control` menu that sets `Input.mouse_mode = MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE`, and move the mouse over it.
4. First open after launch is usually fine; a later open freezes to seconds-per-frame while the mouse moves, recovering after ~20–90 s or after re-capturing the cursor.

I'm happy to run instrumented/patched builds, bisect PRs between 4.7.1 and 4.7.2, or collect more data (ETW, additional stack samples) on request — the reproduction is reliable on this machine.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not yet extracted (private project; the trigger needs a few minutes of gameplay). Will attempt an MRP if the direction above doesn't immediately ring a bell; meanwhile all instrumentation logs (frame-stage breakdowns, stack samples, witness-window logs) are available.
